A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-entanglement study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original TL;DR and curated sentiment experiments, including training trajectories, gradient cosine similarities, and a token-level gradient heatmap.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional DPO training trajectories on UltraFeedback and additional model configurations in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The normalized-gradient update and sparsity-regularized token-masking objective in Section 5 remain substantively unchanged. V2 names them Normalized Preference Optimization and Sparse Preference Optimization without introducing new algorithmic components.

E1.justification: V2 adds DPO experiments using UltraFeedback preference data in Figure 5. TL;DR summarization and all four curated sentiment-response variants are retained, making this a limited extension of the evaluated data coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding TL;DR comparisons retain CPO, DPO, DPOP, IPO, R-DPO, RRHF, SPPO, SimPO, and SLiC-HF. V2's new Figure 5 varies datasets and models for DPO rather than adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: V2's Figure 5 expands the reported model configurations to include Llama3.1-8B, Llama3.2-3B, and Gemma2-9B. The retained experiments' metrics and stated settings are unchanged; the newly specified batch size and epoch count do not establish a changed training budget.

E4.justification: V2 extends the examination of DPO's coupled likelihood dynamics across model configurations and datasets. Section 4.2 also newly reports that Condition 1 is not violated in the synthetic suffix cases despite their observed likelihood decreases. The existing suffix-length and token-correlation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 does not introduce uncertainty reporting for either retained or added results.

E6.justification: V2 adds UltraFeedback and additional-model trajectories in Figure 5 and late-training cosine-similarity points in Figure 4a. It also newly reports the absence of Condition 1 violations in the suffix experiments. The matched TL;DR comparison curves are retained with changed plotting scales.

T1.justification: V1's Corollary 2 guarantees desirable whole-response probability changes when responses differ only at their final token. V2 restricts that guarantee to the differing token and adds Appendix B.2, deriving how shared-prefix contributions can violate the whole-response condition. Appendix A.1 also corrects the gradient-descent signs in the Taylor expansions. This materially revises a formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the central claims: identifying gradient entanglement, deriving gradient conditions, investigating token-level behavior, and outlining two potential mitigation approaches. Naming the approaches does not change their scientific scope or establish their effectiveness.

C2.justification: V1 presents the synthetic observations as validating its gradient-condition analysis. V2 explicitly acknowledges that the conditions remain satisfied in the short- and long-suffix cases despite non-ideal behavior, suggesting first-order approximation error as a possible explanation. Together with the new whole-response qualification following Corollary 2, this substantially narrows the interpretation of the theory's predictive scope.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies an effective batch size of 16 and one training epoch. These are additional disclosures, not documented changes from earlier settings. The software version, hardware, LoRA rank, learning rate, algorithm hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for UltraFeedback, Mistral 7B, and Gemma 2 to support the expanded experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to existing preference-optimization methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation corrections, names the two proposed designs, groups Section 4's theoretical results into subsections, and moves additional empirical results from Appendix C.5 into Appendix D. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the model-by-dataset panel in Figure 5 and gives the existing nine-method plots individual vertical scales. V1's Figures 5 and 6 become Figures 6 and 7 and share the final page; Figure 4a also extends its displayed trajectory. The tables and overall document design are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision by replacing Corollary 2's overbroad whole-response guarantee with a token-level result and adding the prefix analysis. It also acknowledges the empirical condition mismatch, broadens experimental checks, and discloses training details. The gain remains limited because the mismatch is not resolved and earlier statements about ideal behavior and empirical validation are not fully reconciled with the new qualifications.
